claims.text: Gate mode. Writes nothing; returns ``{"ok": bool, "problems": [...]}``.
claims.why: check() never writes; returns dict with 'ok' and 'problems' keys.

claims.text: Four ways to fail, in the order a reader needs them: 1. there is no inventory, or it cannot be parsed; 2. it was written by a different schema; 3. its digest does not cover its own derived fields -- somebody edited the mechanical half by hand; 4. regenerating it now would change something -- it is STALE, and the diff says exactly how.
claims.why: The docstring lists four failure modes but the code checks five conditions: (1) no inventory (stored is None), (2) parse error (__error__), (3) schema mismatch, (4) digest mismatch, (5) annotation overreach. The docstring's first item conflates 'no inventory' and 'cannot be parsed', but the code treats them as separate checks. Also, the docstring's first item is not actually a distinct failure mode in the enumeration; the code's first branch is 'no inventory', which is not listed. The fourth item (stale) is present. The annotation overreach check is not mentioned. Thus the claim of 'four ways' is inaccurate.
No write operations occur in check(); it only reads and builds in memory.
The return statement includes both 'ok' and 'problems' keys.

claims.text: the derived fields do not match the digest written with them: something was hand-edited.
claims.why: The code calls digest_ok(stored) and appends exactly that message when it fails.

claims.text: Pre-seeding a status, an island or a test list is not a way to steer the work queue
claims.why: The comment is present; no contradiction in this chunk.

claims.text: annotation carries fields a human may not set -- {entry}
claims.why: The code appends that exact message for each entry in annotation_overreach.

claims.text: Every feature's DERIVED half, keyed by module (or by detector for the module-less stale entries). The human fields are dropped so a note cannot read as drift.
claims.why: The function iterates areas/features, builds key from module or detector:reason, and filters out FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS.

claims.text: The human fields are dropped so a note cannot read as drift.
claims.why: The comprehension excludes keys in FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS.

claims.text: Field-level, not just status-level. A module whose importers or reaching entry point changed is a real difference, and reporting it as "something differs, go diff the file yourself" is how a gate stops being read.
claims.why: The code compares full derived feature dicts and reports which fields changed, not just status.

claims.text: the derived half differs from a fresh scan (no headline difference; compare the file with --json)
claims.why: When no other differences found, the code appends exactly that message.

claims.text: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run; human notes are carried forward and excluded from the digest.
claims.why: The description matches the behavior seen in refresh() (build + write) and the existence of harvest() which carries forward human notes; the digest exclusion is consistent with digest_ok usage.

claims.text: gate mode: exit non-zero if the file is missing, hand-edited or stale; writes nothing
claims.why: check() returns ok False for those conditions; main returns 1; no writes in check path.

claims.text: print the generated document; writes nothing
claims.why: The --json branch builds a doc and prints it; no write occurs.
